# Solar watts to recharge a 1,000Wh power station

**For a full recharge in about one day, plan on roughly 300-400W of panels.** If you can wait a day and a half or two, 200W works.

## The math
Daily solar energy is panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75, which covers heat, angle and charging losses. Rearranged, panel watts = 1,000 Wh ÷ (sun hours × ~0.7-0.75).

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts for a 1-day recharge |
|---|---|
| 3 (winter, cloudy) | ~450W ([source](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |
| 4 | ~340W ([source](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |
| 5 | ~270W ([source](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |
| 6 (summer, Southwest) | ~230W ([source](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)) |

- **200W panel:** about 630 Wh/day at 4.5 sun hours, so a little over a day and a half to fill from empty ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Rule of thumb:** battery Wh ÷ 5 gives about 200W for a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Winter in the northern US:** about 2 peak sun hours, which means roughly 700W+ for a one-day refill ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

## Check before you buy
- **Solar input limit:** your station caps how many watts it accepts. Mid-range 1,000-1,500Wh units often allow 400-800W, but some cap at 200W, and extra panel beyond the cap adds little ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage:** the panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the station. Wiring panels in series adds voltage, so parallel is the safer default ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Using power while charging:** any load you run during the day reduces the net recharge.

## A panel option
The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) fits the one-day goal at about 3+ peak sun hours. It lists 37.4 V Vmp and 45.3 V Voc, with MC4 connectors and XT60/DC adapters included.

- **Compatible:** stations with 12-60V solar inputs, such as the BLUETTI AC180 and AC200L or the ALLPOWERS P1800.
- **Not compatible:** the Tenergy T320 and BLUETTI Elite 30 V2, because their input voltage limits are too low.
- **Weight:** 18.5 kg, which is heavy for a folding panel.
- **Price:** $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 through 2026-12-30 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/how-many-watts-solar-panel-to-recharge-1000wh-portable-power-station-solar-charg)).

That is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. Confirm your station's max solar watts and voltage range first. If you tell me the model, I can check whether this panel suits it or suggest a size.
